# Nonregular concave-parameter stationarity and an actual base-volume martingale

This is an UNPENALIZED parameter theorem at an actual joint local minimum. It does not require regular cap derivatives, singleton faces, or an actual physical-response separator. Its weights sigma must not be identified with physical eta unless an additional common-separator theorem supplies that identification.

The new step is the exact exclusion of a parameter direction strictly lowering every proper deepest base, using scalar monotonicity and the actual all-atomic hinge cleanup. Once that step is proved, the finite tangent/Farkas/absorption argument is the already audited mechanism of `candidate cfe4a95984691190`.

## 1. Setting and hypotheses

Fix a finite lattice-complete canonical base P, d>=1, positive compatible fibers K_z, total mass M, and weights w_z=|K_z|/M. Let k=k(P). Take epsilon>0 and a positive sampled-concave array ell, normalized by

    sum_z w_z log ell_z=0.

Use its canonical concave roof and the affine-invariant buffered depth with f=(ell E/M)^(1/(d+1)) and the actual within-fiber covariance norm. Let Q>0 be the maximal raw buffered depth at sampled sources and beta=Q/M. Assume the body/parameter pair is a genuine JOINT LOCAL minimum over positive compatible bodies on this fixed base and all positive normalized sampled-concave arrays. Assume

    beta<1/k.                                           (1)

The hypothetical OC-bad regime beta<Gamma_d/k is a special case. The objective here has NO multiplier penalty.

Let I be the actual deepest bases and set

    J={p in I:b_base(p)>Q},
    A=I outside J.

The existing all-atomic hinge theorem excludes J empty under (1), so J is nonempty. No regularity or uniqueness of the deepest mark within a base is assumed.

Let T_ell be the exact one-sided tangent cone of sampled concavity. It consists of arrays h satisfying

    h_p>=sum_z lambda_z h_z                              (2)

for every ell-tight extreme anchored representation of p. There are finitely many such inequalities. Every fixed h in this cone makes ell+t h positive and sampled-concave for all sufficiently small positive t.

## 2. The geometric no-improvement statement

For fixed bodies, write

    B_p(h)=h_p/ell_p-sum_z w_z h_z/ell_z.                 (3)

There is NO h in T_ell for which B_p(h)<0 at every p in J.

To prove this, suppose such h exists and normalize the actual raw array ell+t h by its weighted geometric mean. The normalized array ell_t is positive sampled-concave and satisfies

    dot ell_t(p)/ell_p=B_p(h).

Consequently ell_t(p)<ell_p for every p in J and every sufficiently small positive t. The fixed-body maximal buffered depth at a base depends on the multiplier only through that base's single value ell_p.

At each p in J its old maximum is positive and strictly below atomic depth. The already proved scalar strict-monotonicity lemma then makes the NEW whole-fiber maximum strictly smaller than Q. This assertion is nonregular: if an old and a reduced multiplier gave the same maximum, a maximizing mark for the reduced multiplier would also maximize the old one; an attained old active cap has a proper OWN trace and loses positive own volume under the increased threshold. Other fibers can only lose mass. No supporting-cap derivative or uniform coarea estimate is used.

At every p in A, an unchanged pure-base cap of mass Q bounds ALL new marks by Q, independently of their new buffer values. At each p outside I, the old strict gap persists for small t by the fixed-body uniform buffered-depth continuity; there are only finitely many sampled bases. Thus the new global maximum Q_t is at most Q and no old proper base is deepest at value Q.

If Q_t<Q, this is already a strict parameter improvement, contradicting the local minimum. Otherwise Q_t=Q and EVERY new deepest base is an old atomic base, with atomic depth Q. Apply the actual all-atomic convex-base-hinge erosion at this new pair. It produces an arbitrarily small compatible body change strictly lowering normalized depth, because beta<1/k implies beta m<1 for its compressed atomic cover. Normalize the SAME sampled-concave raw array with the new positive body masses; positive scalar normalization preserves sampled concavity. All updated covariance, energy and normalization terms are allowed by the exact hinge theorem.

Both steps can be chosen inside the original local-minimum neighborhood. The second step does not assume that the intervening pair is a new local minimum. It is an actual strict improvement from an equal-value pair. This proves the no-improvement statement without a neutral-path inference.

## 3. Finite parameter separation

The image

    { (B_p(h))_(p in J):h in T_ell }

is a convex polyhedral cone. By the statement just proved it misses the open strictly negative orthant. Finite cone separation therefore supplies

    sigma_p>=0 (p in J),     sum_(p in J) sigma_p=1,

such that

    sum_(p in J) sigma_p B_p(h)>=0
                                  for every h in T_ell. (4)

Equivalently define actual finite BASE measures

    mu=sum_(p in J) (sigma_p/ell_p) delta_p,
    nu=sum_(z in P) (w_z/ell_z) delta_z.                  (5)

Then

    <mu-nu,h>>=0 for every h in T_ell.                   (6)

Every target coefficient is strictly positive. Affine arrays and their negatives belong to T_ell, so (6) gives equal mass and first base moment. Both ell moments equal one directly from (5). These statements retain the original fiber volumes; no restriction to deepest-fiber mass has been made.

## 4. The exact ell-tight volume martingale

Finite Farkas duality writes

    mu-nu=sum_e tau_e(e_(p_e)-lambda_e),   tau_e>=0,       (7)

over the tight rows in (2). Put out_p=sum_(e:p_e=p)tau_e and in_p=sum_e tau_e lambda_(e,p). Then

    mu_p+in_p=nu_p+out_p=:m_p>0.

At each visit to p, absorb with probability nu_p/m_p and otherwise make the anchored transition encoded by the outgoing lambda rows. Finiteness and strict positivity of every nu_p give a uniform positive stopping probability. Therefore all injected mass is absorbed, and the unique visit solution is m. The absorbed target marginal is exactly nu.

Each transition preserves base position and ell in conditional expectation. Bounded stopped martingales thus give a nonnegative coupling pi from mu to nu with

    sum_z pi_(pz) z=mu_p p,
    sum_z pi_(pz) ell_z=mu_p ell_p                     (8)

for every positive source row. This is an actual finite ell-tight BASE martingale and implies mu<=_cx nu. For any selected supporting affine plane of the concave ell roof at a source, all its positive targets lie on that same contact plane.

The construction is valid without cap regularity, source-section measures, response coefficients delta, or a differentiable maximum-depth envelope. It remains a parameter-only consequence. The anchored relations in (8) imply the true Minkowski inclusions of the original fibers, but not equality, centroid matching, a uniform-fiber lift, or a physical supporting-face coupling.

## 5. Exact consequences and limitations

Testing affine functions shows that

    (sum_z w_z z/ell_z)/(sum_z w_z/ell_z) in conv(J),     (9)

recovering the earlier regularity-free tilted-barycenter condition and strengthening it to full convex order and labeled ell contacts.

At least one positively weighted source is a NONVERTEX of conv(P). Otherwise every source row of the martingale is forced to be the identity. Positivity of the full target then makes every sampled base a vertex. Lattice completeness makes those vertices parity-distinct, so k=|P|. A largest-fiber centroid already supplies ordinary raw depth at least Gamma_d M/k and buffered depth no smaller. In particular this contradicts the OC-bad hypothesis beta<Gamma_d/k. Thus the nonvertex conclusion uses that stronger bad threshold, not merely (1).

More generally, if every nontrivial anchored relation at every positively weighted source has strict ell Jensen inequality, all rows are again identities. Then every base is a proper source and sigma_p=w_p pointwise. This exact conditional rigidity requires the stated strictness and does not follow just from positive concavity.

In a regular-singleton mixed covering setting, the earlier COMMON physical/parameter separator can instead choose

    sigma_p=Delta^(-1) sum_(i:p_i=p) eta_i delta_i,

where Delta>0 is ensured by atomic hinge cleanup in the same physical cone. That special choice belongs simultaneously to the physical certificate. The abstract separator (4) need not be that choice, and the present nonregular proof does NOT identify it with any surface Jordan coupling.

The safe three-interval calibration from the audited companion theorem remains valid: even at the unique full-concave parameter optimum, the base-volume target can lie outside the deepest/finite-threshold domain and cannot be lifted with uniform conditional fiber distributions. The present theorem therefore removes regularity from the arithmetic transport, not from the physical response or Gamma payment problem.

## 6. Dependencies and scope

The actual geometric inputs are the sampled strict-base-gap scalar monotonicity, positive-family depth continuity, and `candidate f324bc23ceb65e89`. The finite cone and absorption proof is the audited companion `candidate cfe4a95984691190` with Delta normalized to one.

No penalty term is discarded. With a multiplier penalty, the no-improvement implication of Section 2 need not hold, and both the transport marginals and the hinge comparison require their genuine extra terms.
